claims.claim: Lower-dose amoxicillin was noninferior to higher-dose therapy for 28-day respiratory antibiotic retreatment.
Three-day therapy was noninferior to seven-day therapy for the same primary endpoint.
The noninferiority margin was revised from 4% to 8% after the internal pilot showed a materially higher retreatment rate than originally assumed.
The severe-CAP subgroup did not establish noninferiority for lower versus higher dose, while the duration comparison remained within the 8% margin.
Cough and sleep-disturbance resolution favored 7 days in exploratory analyses, with an internal abstract/results CI-level discrepancy.
Serious adverse events occurred in 5%; adherence to active therapy was higher with 3-day than 7-day treatment.
No penicillin-resistant pneumococci were detected at day 28, and nonsusceptibility did not differ significantly by randomized dose or duration.
Generalizability is limited for very severe disease, major comorbidity, and prolonged inpatient treatment.
